suggestions.title: Fill in Thursday — rough numbers are fine. It is the day the scale finally moved and the only day with nothing behind it.

rationale.science: When a rate stalls, check adherence and logging before blaming metabolism — the logging gap is the first thing to rule out, not the last (Alhassan 2008).
rationale.data: 8/13 has a weight read of 163.3 and nothing else: no calories, protein, sodium or steps in dailyLogs, no entry in sleep.nights for Wednesday night, and no session on an upper day. 8/12 sodium is still blank too.
rationale.relationship: Monday 8/17 is when the rate window finally empties of the 8/5-8/8 maintenance days, and I committed to a real test on it — under 0.6 lb/wk with a clean window means the deficit is not what I think and the food log is wrong. A missing Thursday sits inside that window and makes the test unanswerable either way.

suggestions.predict: Fill it in and Monday's rate is a verdict I can be wrong about. Leave it blank and Monday's number cannot be assigned to the body or to the bookkeeping, and this week's argument closes without an answer.

suggestions.title: Ham curl: check in SETUP that the machine actually makes 125 before you load it today.

rationale.science: On a cut, defend load — a progression you have to retract costs more than the one you never took (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024).
rationale.data: q_ham_125 is state DEBUT, done false, earned off 120 x 12,12,11 on 8/10. Today is your lower day under the split you set on 8/9 (Fri = L), so it is the first day it is actually due.
rationale.relationship: The hack ladder went wrong in exactly this way — a rung assumed rather than checked, then a retracted earn. Ten seconds in SETUP either confirms 125 exists or tells you the real next rung before you build a session on it.

suggestions.predict: If 125 is a real rung, it debuts today and q_ham_125 closes clean. If it is not, you find out standing at the machine instead of two sessions later, and the queue gets the honest number.

suggestions.title: One short night, worth naming: 02:30 to bed on Tuesday put your sleep debt back on the board after eleven clean days.

rationale.science: At matched deficits, short sleep cut fat loss about 55% and raised lean-mass loss about 60% — it is a first-order body-composition lever, not a footnote (Nedeltcheva 2010; Wang 2018).
rationale.data: 8/12 night: bed 02:30, 5.33 h — against 23:55 and 7.67 h the night before. Seven-night debt went 0 to 1.7 h on that one night; twelve-night mean is 6.9 h. Wednesday night was never logged.
rationale.relationship: It is one night out of five and four of the five were good, so this is a flag and not an alarm. What makes it worth saying is the sequence: the short night sits directly in front of the blank Thursday and the skipped upper session. That is the ordinary way a bad night costs you — through the day after, not through your metabolism.

suggestions.predict: Back to a midnight-ish bedtime tonight and the seven-night debt is under 1.0 h by Sunday. Your sleep target is already 7.5 h so there is nothing to change and no button here — the target was never the problem, and if the debt keeps climbing on logged nights then this ask is wrong and I will stop making it.
